mission_08: Outstanding work implementing a comprehensive anomaly detection toolkit! You now have four complementary approaches for identifying unusual patterns in time series data. The z-score method provides a simple, interpretable baseline for point anomaly detection. CUSUM excels at detecting gradual shifts and change points that accumulate over time, making it ideal for monitoring processes. The isolation forest brings a machine learning perspective, using random partitioning to identify points that are inherently different from the bulk of the data. Seasonal anomaly detection accounts for periodic patterns, ensuring that normal seasonal peaks are not falsely flagged as anomalies. Together, these methods cover the major categories of time series anomalies: point anomalies, contextual anomalies, collective anomalies, and seasonal deviations. This toolkit is directly applicable to real-world monitoring systems in manufacturing, IT operations, finance, and healthcare.
